newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CMN to mull Minas Gerais bank selloff.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CMN to mull Minas Gerais bank selloff.

text.p: Brazil's National Monetary Council was due to meet at 1500 local/1700 GMT to discuss plans by Minas Gerais state to privatize its banks, an official said.
The CMN, Brazil's highest monetary policy body, would also study new rules for public sector pension funds, he said.
Minas Gerais intends to privatize its banks Credireal and Banco do Estado de Minas Gerais and liquidate mortgage bank Minas Caixa.
The state hopes to secure financing of about 2.5 billion reais from Brasilia to clean up the three banks' balance sheets.

The financing would be provided under a federal government program to help states clear up the debts of their banks. States that privatize or liquidate their banks qualify for financing equivalent to 100 percent of the debts while those that opt to maintain control may receive 50 percent.
Newspapers said the CMN would also study new rules for public sector pension funds that would oblige the funds to diversify their investments to reduce risk.
